explanation: Erdős #1195: how fast can |S ∩ (0,x)| grow for measurable S of infinite measure with no integer ratios x/y? The site records Ho Boon Suan–GPT's resolution: for non-decreasing F → ∞, such S with |S ∩ (0,x)| ≥ F(x) exists iff ∫₁^∞ F(x)/x² dx < ∞. The Lean characterises the set of growth rates admitting such S as exactly those with F/x² integrable on [1,∞). For non-negative F this is equivalent to finiteness of the integral. A Lean proof is linked. The statement is correct and solved.
